title: Bali's Temple Monkeys Steal Phones, Then Trade Them Back for Food

scenes.text: At one temple in Bali, the monkeys run a ransom business.
The long-tailed macaques at Uluwatu snatch things from visitors: hats, sunglasses, phones. Then they sit just out of reach, and wait.
People offer food. The monkey lets go only when the offer is good enough.
Researchers filmed them for 273 days and found they know what's valuable. For a phone or a pair of glasses, they hold out for more.
A banana might buy back a hat. A phone can cost you an egg.
Young monkeys steal anything and bargain badly. The skill grows with age, and it's been handed down for generations.

description:
At Uluwatu Temple in Bali, long-tailed macaques steal visitors' belongings and give them back only in exchange for food.
A study led by Jean-Baptiste Leca of the University of Lethbridge, filmed over 273 days in 2015 and 2016, found that the monkeys match their price to the item: phones, tablets and glasses are held for better rewards than hats or empty bags. The skill improves with age and has been passed down for decades.
What would a monkey get from you?
subject: long-tailed macaque
first_comment: The study, in a Royal Society journal, calls it robbing and bartering. What's the one thing you'd pay a monkey anything to get back?
